## Classes

### <a name="manage_opensearch"></a>`manage_opensearch`

Include this class on every OpenSearch node that should report the
`opensearch` fact or manage `opensearch_*` resources. It writes the
connection settings to `/etc/puppetlabs/manage_opensearch/connections.yaml`
(owner root, mode 0600). The top-level parameters describe the connection
named `default`. `connections` adds more named connections, which resources
select with their `connection` parameter.

#### Examples

##### Connect to the local node with basic auth

```puppet
class { 'manage_opensearch':
  username => 'admin',
  password => Sensitive('secret'),
  ca_file  => '/etc/opensearch/root-ca.pem',
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `manage_opensearch` class:

* [`url`](#-manage_opensearch--url)
* [`username`](#-manage_opensearch--username)
* [`password`](#-manage_opensearch--password)
* [`ca_file`](#-manage_opensearch--ca_file)
* [`client_cert`](#-manage_opensearch--client_cert)
* [`client_key`](#-manage_opensearch--client_key)
* [`verify_tls`](#-manage_opensearch--verify_tls)
* [`timeout`](#-manage_opensearch--timeout)

* [`connections`](#-manage_opensearch--connections)

### <a name="opensearch_alias"></a>`opensearch_alias`

Changes are made in one atomic `_aliases` request: an alias never points
to no index or to both the old and the new one. `filter`, the routing
values and `is_hidden` apply to all indices of the alias.

Don't manage aliases that ISM rolls over (`rollover_alias`): ISM moves
the write index and Puppet would move it back. Aliases whose name starts
with a dot are not listed. The title is either the alias name or
`connection/name`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_alias { 'orders':
  indices     => ['orders-2025', 'orders-2026'],
  write_index => 'orders-2026',
}

opensearch_alias { 'orders-eu':
  indices => ['orders-2025', 'orders-2026'],
  filter  => { 'term' => { 'region' => 'eu' } },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_alias` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the alias should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `filter`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

A query that limits the documents visible through the alias.

##### `index_routing`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Routing value for writes through the alias.

##### `indices`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Pattern[/\A[^*,]+\z/], 1]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The indices the alias points to; names, no wildcards. The order does not matter. Required when creating the alias.

##### `is_hidden`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether the alias is left out of wildcard expressions.

##### `search_routing`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Routing values (comma-separated) for searches through the alias.

##### `write_index`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The index that receives writes to the alias. Must be one of `indices`.

### <a name="opensearch_allowlist"></a>`opensearch_allowlist`

When the allow list is enabled, users other than the super admin can only
call the listed endpoints with the listed methods.

The allow list exists once per cluster, so the title is the name of a
connection from the class `manage_opensearch`. **The connection must use
the admin certificate** (`client_cert` and `client_key`); with a user and
password, OpenSearch denies access even for `admin`. Listing
(`puppet resource opensearch_allowlist`) skips connections without access.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
class { 'manage_opensearch':
  username    => 'admin',
  password    => Sensitive('secret'),
  connections => {
    'superadmin' => {
      'url'         => "https://${facts['networking']['fqdn']}:9200",
      'client_cert' => '/etc/opensearch/admin.pem',
      'client_key'  => '/etc/opensearch/admin-key.pem',
      'ca_file'     => '/etc/opensearch/root-ca.pem',
    },
  },
}

opensearch_allowlist { 'superadmin':
  enabled  => true,
  requests => {
    '/_cluster/health' => ['GET'],
    '/_cat/nodes'      => ['GET'],
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_allowlist` type.

##### `enabled`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether the allow list is enforced.

##### `requests`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String[1], Array[Enum['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', 'PATCH', 'HEAD']]]]`

Allowed requests: endpoint path => HTTP methods. The order of the methods does not matter.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_allowlist` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_allowlist--connection)

##### <a name="-opensearch_allowlist--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use. It must use the admin certificate.

### <a name="opensearch_data_stream"></a>`opensearch_data_stream`

Creating a data stream needs an index template with `data_stream` whose
`index_patterns` match the name. The data stream automatically depends on
an `opensearch_index_template` with the same name. An ISM policy whose
`ism_template` matches the data stream name must exist before the data
stream, so that it applies to the first backing index; add a `require`.

Creating the data stream in advance means that the applications that
write to it only need write permissions, not `indices:admin/create`.

**`ensure => absent` deletes the data stream with all its backing indices
and data.** So does purging with `resources`, for every data stream not in
the catalog, including those that applications created themselves. Data
streams whose name starts with a dot are not listed.

The title is either the name or `connection/name`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_data_stream { 'metrics':
  require => Opensearch_ism_policy['metrics_daily'],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_data_stream` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the data stream should exist. `absent` deletes all its data.

Default value: `present`

##### `generation`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

The number of the current backing index, i.e. rollovers + 1 (read only).

##### `template`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The index template the data stream was created from (read only).

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_data_stream` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_data_stream--connection)
* [`name`](#-opensearch_data_stream--name)

##### <a name="-opensearch_data_stream--connection"></a>`connection`

_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

Default value: `default`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The name of the data stream.

### <a name="opensearch_index"></a>`opensearch_index`

whether it is open.

Prefer index templates and data streams for indices that are created
continuously; use this type for single, long-lived indices.

* `settings` and `mappings` are in sync when everything they contain is
  present in the index with the same value. Settings may be nested or
  dotted, with or without the `index.` prefix.
* Changed settings are updated in place. Static settings (e.g. `codec`)
  can only be changed on a closed index: set `state => closed`, and the
  index is closed before the settings are changed. `number_of_shards`
  can never be changed.
* New mapping fields are added; the type of an existing field cannot be
  changed (OpenSearch rejects it).
* Aliases are managed with `opensearch_alias`.
* **`ensure => absent` deletes the index and its data**, and so does
  purging. Indices starting with a dot (system indices, backing indices
  of data streams) and hidden indices are not listed or purged.

The title is either the index name or `connection/name`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_index { 'customers':
  settings => { 'number_of_shards' => 1, 'number_of_replicas' => 1, 'refresh_interval' => '5s' },
  mappings => {
    'dynamic'    => 'strict',
    'properties' => {
      'name'  => { 'type' => 'text' },
      'email' => { 'type' => 'keyword' },
    },
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_index` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the index should exist. `absent` deletes its data.

Default value: `present`

##### `mappings`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Mappings (`properties`, `dynamic`, ...). Only the mappings given here are compared.

##### `settings`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Index settings. Only the settings given here are compared.

##### `state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum[open, closed]]`

Whether the index is open or closed. A closed index cannot be read or written.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_index` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_index--connection)
* [`name`](#-opensearch_index--name)

##### <a name="-opensearch_index--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use.

Default value: `default`

##### <a name="-opensearch_index--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^*,"<>|\/\\\\? #A-Z]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The name of the index: lowercase, without spaces and the characters * , " < > | / \\ ? #.

### <a name="opensearch_index_template"></a>`opensearch_index_template`

Index settings may be nested or dotted, with or without the `index.`
prefix, and with numbers or strings: `{ 'number_of_shards' => 1 }` and
`{ 'index' => { 'number_of_shards' => '1' } }` are the same. Attributes
that are not set are kept as they are in the cluster. The title is either
the name or `connection/name`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_index_template { 'logs':
  index_patterns => ['logs-*'],
  priority       => 100,
  template       => {
    'settings' => { 'number_of_shards' => 1, 'refresh_interval' => '5s' },
    'mappings' => { 'properties' => { 'message' => { 'type' => 'text' } } },
    'aliases'  => { 'logs' => {} },
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_index_template` type.

##### `composed_of`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Component templates, merged in this order.

##### `data_stream`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Makes the template create data streams; `{}` uses the default timestamp field `@timestamp`.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the index template should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `index_patterns`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1], 1]]`

Index name patterns the template applies to. Required when creating the template.

##### `meta`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Free-form metadata (`_meta` in the API).

##### `priority`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

Templates with a higher priority win when several match an index.

##### `template`

Data type: `Optional[Struct[{Optional[settings] => Hash, Optional[mappings] => Hash, Optional[aliases] => Hash}]]`

Settings, mappings and aliases of new indices.

##### `version`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

A version number for your own bookkeeping.

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_index_template` type.

### <a name="opensearch_ingest_pipeline"></a>`opensearch_ingest_pipeline`

Processors are compared exactly, in their order. Attributes that are not
set are kept as they are in the cluster. The title is either the ID or
`connection/ID`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_ingest_pipeline { 'metrics_enrich':
  description => 'Adds the environment and parses the level',
  processors  => [
    { 'set' => { 'field' => 'environment', 'value' => 'production' } },
    { 'lowercase' => { 'field' => 'level', 'ignore_missing' => true } },
  ],
  on_failure  => [
    { 'set' => { 'field' => 'ingest_error', 'value' => '{{ _ingest.on_failure_message }}' } },
  ],
}
```

### <a name="opensearch_internal_user"></a>`opensearch_internal_user`

The password (or its bcrypt hash) is only used when the user is created.
After that it is ignored: changing it in the manifest does not change the
user, and a password changed in OpenSearch is not reset.

Built-in (reserved, static or hidden) users are not listed and cannot be
changed. The title is either the name or `connection/name`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_internal_user { 'logstash':
  password                  => Sensitive('initial-secret'),
  backend_roles             => ['logstash'],
  opendistro_security_roles => ['logs_writer'],
  attributes                => { 'team' => 'ops' },
}
```

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_internal_user` type.

##### `attributes`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String[1], Scalar]]`

Custom attributes, usable e.g. in document-level security queries. Values are stored as strings.

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Backend roles of the user.

##### `description`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

A description of the user.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the user should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `opendistro_security_roles`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Roles assigned to the user directly, without a role mapping.

##### `password`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

The initial password. Only used when the user is created, never compared afterwards.

### <a name="opensearch_ism_policy"></a>`opensearch_ism_policy`

OpenSearch adds defaults to stored policies (e.g. `retry` settings for
every action). `states`, `ism_template` and `error_notification` are
therefore in sync when everything the manifest specifies is present in
the cluster with the same value. Extra keys added by the server are
ignored. Lists must have the same length and order.

Updating a policy does not change indices that are already managed by an
older version of it. The title is either the policy id or
`connection/policy_id`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_ism_policy { 'logs_retention':
  description   => 'Delete log indices after 30 days',
  default_state => 'hot',
  states        => [
    {
      'name'        => 'hot',
      'actions'     => [{ 'rollover' => { 'min_size' => '10gb' } }],
      'transitions' => [{ 'state_name' => 'delete', 'conditions' => { 'min_index_age' => '30d' } }],
    },
    { 'name' => 'delete', 'actions' => [{ 'delete' => {} }], 'transitions' => [] },
  ],
  ism_template  => [{ 'index_patterns' => ['logs-*'], 'priority' => 100 }],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_ism_policy` type.

##### `default_state`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The state new indices start in. Required when creating the policy.

##### `description`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

A description of the policy.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the ISM policy should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `error_notification`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Where to send a notification when a managed index fails.

##### `ism_template`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Hash]]`

Index patterns (with priority) whose new indices get this policy automatically.

##### `states`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Hash, 1]]`

The states with their actions and transitions, as in the ISM API.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_ism_policy` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_ism_policy--connection)
* [`name`](#-opensearch_ism_policy--name)

##### <a name="-opensearch_ism_policy--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use.

Default value: `default`

##### <a name="-opensearch_ism_policy--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The name of the ISM policy.

### <a name="opensearch_role"></a>`opensearch_role`

Built-in (reserved, static or hidden) roles are not listed and cannot be
changed. The order of permissions does not matter. The title is either the
name or `connection/name`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_role { 'logs_reader':
  cluster_permissions => ['cluster_composite_ops_ro'],
  index_permissions   => [
    {
      index_patterns  => ['logs-*'],
      allowed_actions => ['read'],
      fls             => ['~secret_field'],
    },
  ],
  tenant_permissions  => [
    { tenant_patterns => ['logs'], allowed_actions => ['kibana_all_read'] },
  ],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_role` type.

### <a name="opensearch_role_mapping"></a>`opensearch_role_mapping`

The name is the name of the role. A mapping autorequires the
`opensearch_role` of the same name. The title is either the role name or
`connection/role`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_role_mapping { 'logs_reader':
  backend_roles => ['ldap-logs-readers'],
  users         => ['alice'],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_role_mapping` type.

##### `and_backend_roles`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Backend roles that a user must all have to get the role.

##### `backend_roles`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Backend roles (e.g. LDAP groups) that get the role.

##### `description`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

A description of the mapping.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the role mapping should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `hosts`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Hosts whose requests get the role.

##### `users`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Users that get the role.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_role_mapping` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_role_mapping--connection)
* [`name`](#-opensearch_role_mapping--name)

##### <a name="-opensearch_role_mapping--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use.

Default value: `default`

##### <a name="-opensearch_role_mapping--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The name of the role mapping.

### <a name="opensearch_search_pipeline"></a>`opensearch_search_pipeline`

Processors are compared exactly, in their order. Attributes that are not
set are kept as they are in the cluster. The title is either the ID or
`connection/ID`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_search_pipeline { 'public_only':
  description        => 'Only returns public documents',
  request_processors => [
    { 'filter_query' => { 'query' => { 'term' => { 'visibility' => 'public' } } } },
  ],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_search_pipeline` type.

##### `description`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

A description of the pipeline.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the pipeline should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `phase_results_processors`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Hash[String[1], Hash]]]`

Processors that run between the query and fetch phases, e.g. `normalization-processor` for hybrid search.

##### `request_processors`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Hash[String[1], Hash]]]`

Processors that change the search request, in the order they run.

##### `response_processors`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Hash[String[1], Hash]]]`

Processors that change the search response, in the order they run.

##### `version`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

A version number for your own bookkeeping.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_search_pipeline` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_search_pipeline--connection)
* [`name`](#-opensearch_search_pipeline--name)

##### <a name="-opensearch_search_pipeline--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use.

Default value: `default`

##### <a name="-opensearch_search_pipeline--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The ID of the pipeline.

### <a name="opensearch_stored_script"></a>`opensearch_stored_script`

A search template (`lang => 'mustache'`) may be given as a Hash; it is
compared with the stored template as data, not as text. Attributes that
are not set are kept as they are in the cluster. The title is either the
ID or `connection/ID`.

#### Examples

##### A Painless script, compiled for the score context when stored

```puppet
opensearch_stored_script { 'boost_by_popularity':
  lang    => 'painless',
  source  => "_score * Math.log(2 + doc['popularity'].value)",
  context => 'score',
}
```

##### A search template

```puppet
opensearch_stored_script { 'find_by_host':
  lang   => 'mustache',
  source => {
    'query' => { 'term' => { 'host.name' => '{{host}}' } },
    'size'  => '{{size}}',
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_stored_script` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the script should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `lang`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The script language, e.g. `painless` or `mustache`. Required when creating the script.

##### `source`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String[1], Hash]]`

The script. For `mustache`, a Hash with the search request or a JSON string. Required when creating the script.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_stored_script` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_stored_script--connection)
* [`context`](#-opensearch_stored_script--context)
* [`name`](#-opensearch_stored_script--name)

##### <a name="-opensearch_stored_script--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use.

Default value: `default`

##### <a name="-opensearch_stored_script--context"></a>`context`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

A script context such as `score` or `filter`. If set, OpenSearch compiles the script when storing it and rejects invalid
scripts. Not stored, so not compared.

##### <a name="-opensearch_stored_script--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The ID of the script.

### <a name="opensearch_tenancy_config"></a>`opensearch_tenancy_config`

The configuration exists once per cluster, so the title is the name of a
connection from the class `manage_opensearch`. It cannot be removed.
Attributes that are not set are kept as they are in the cluster.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_tenancy_config { 'default':
  multitenancy_enabled   => true,
  private_tenant_enabled => false,
  default_tenant         => 'operations',
  preferred_tenants      => ['operations', 'global_tenant'],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_tenancy_config` type.

##### `default_tenant`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The tenant OpenSearch Dashboards opens by default. It must exist.

##### `multitenancy_enabled`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether multi-tenancy is enabled in OpenSearch Dashboards.

##### `preferred_tenants`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Tenants listed first in the tenant selector, in this order. OpenSearch 3 and later.

##### `private_tenant_enabled`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether users have a private tenant.

##### `sign_in_options`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['BASIC', 'SAML', 'OPENID', 'ANONYMOUS']]]`

Sign-in options shown by OpenSearch Dashboards. Each needs a matching authentication domain. The order does not matter.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_tenancy_config` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_tenancy_config--connection)

##### <a name="-opensearch_tenancy_config--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use.

### <a name="opensearch_tenant"></a>`opensearch_tenant`

Built-in (reserved, static or hidden) tenants such as `global_tenant` are
not listed and cannot be changed. The title is either the name or
`connection/name`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
opensearch_tenant { 'operations':
  description => 'Dashboards of the operations team',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `opensearch_tenant` type.

##### `description`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

A description of the tenant.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the tenant should exist.

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `opensearch_tenant` type.

* [`connection`](#-opensearch_tenant--connection)
* [`name`](#-opensearch_tenant--name)

##### <a name="-opensearch_tenant--connection"></a>`connection`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The connection from the class manage_opensearch to use.

Default value: `default`

##### <a name="-opensearch_tenant--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The name of the tenant.

## Data types

### <a name="Manage_opensearch--Connection"></a>`Manage_opensearch::Connection`

Settings of one connection to an OpenSearch cluster

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
{
  'url'      => 'https://os1.example.com:9200',
  'username' => 'admin',
  'password' => Sensitive('secret'),
  'ca_file'  => '/etc/opensearch/root-ca.pem',
}
```

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  url                   => Pattern[/\Ahttps?:\/\/\S+\z/],
  Optional[username]    => String[1],
  Optional[password]    => Variant[String[1], Sensitive[String[1]]],
  Optional[ca_file]     => Pattern[/\A\//],
  Optional[client_cert] => Pattern[/\A\//],
  Optional[client_key]  => Pattern[/\A\//],
  Optional[verify_tls]  => Boolean,
  Optional[timeout]     => Integer[1],
  Optional[retries]     => Integer[0],
}]
```
